messages:
nina: Running a quick sweep comparing steady-state coalescer vs default timer across H100 (us-west, eu-west) and L4 (apac-northeast). Shared p50/p95 and throughput numbers below — p95 on apac-H100 spikes with current max_token_cap=2048. Anyone seen similar regional kernel variance?

raj: can you paste the exact config + how you measured? Was this with int8 quant or fp16?

nina: fp16 for H100, int8 for L4. Measurement: 30m steady load, synthetic chat traffic (mean len 60). Script:
```
perf/run_bench.py --model mosaic-13b --quant fp16 --gpu h100 --region us-west --batch-timer-ms 12 --max-tokens 2048 --duration 1800
```

emily: nice — results from last run (trimmed):
```
us-west H100: p50=18ms p95=72ms tokens/s=450k
eu-west H100: p50=20ms p95=85ms tokens/s=420k
apac L4 int8: p50=26ms p95=210ms tokens/s=380k
```
apac p95 looks like microburst queuing on kernel selector fallback.

tom: try lowering batch-timer to 6ms and add max_batch_tokens=4096 for H100, for L4 try tighter fairshare for long requests: decay=0.6

nina: ran tom's config overnight, quick summary:
```
batch-timer=6ms, max_batch_tokens=4096 -> apac p95 dropped to 120ms, tokens/s +8% on H100
fairshare decay=0.6 -> latency tail improved for long-tail users but throughput ~ -2%
```

raj: can you push the perf logs + kernel selection trace? need to see if it switched kernels when seq len > 512.

perf-bot: Uploaded artifact: s3://redwood-perf/1903123456/kernel-traces.tar.gz :package:

nina: linked artifacts and a short notebook with charts: https://internal.redwood/s/bench/1903123456

emily: next steps: run a controlled quantization sweep (fp16 vs int8) on apac H100 and add KV cache warmup to warm up prefixes — might fix p95.

tom: also consider routing policy: prefer h100-region fallback when request len>1024.

nina: thanks all, will run the quant sweep tomorrow and post quick diff. :thumbsup:
